question: A 6-year-old girl's peripheral blood smear shows hypochromic microcytic red cells, occasional target cells, pencil cells, and a markedly elevated RDW. Her serum ferritin is 4 µg/L (low). Which diagnosis does this smear-ferritin combination most strongly support?

answers.text: Beta-thalassaemia trait — microcytic with target cells, low-normal ferritin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Beta-thalassaemia trait also shows microcytosis and target cells, but ferritin is typically normal and RDW is usually normal or only mildly elevated. A very low ferritin with high RDW is characteristic of IDA, not thalassaemia trait.

answers.text: Iron deficiency anaemia — hypochromic microcytic with high RDW and very low ferritin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. IDA smear: hypochromia, microcytosis, pencil cells (elliptocytes), target cells, high RDW (anisocytosis). Very low ferritin (<12 µg/L in children) confirms depleted iron stores. The combination of high RDW + low ferritin distinguishes IDA from thalassaemia trait (which has normal RDW and ferritin).

answers.text: G6PD deficiency — bite cells and Heinz bodies with normal ferritin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: G6PD deficiency shows bite cells and Heinz bodies (on supravital stain) during haemolytic episodes. There are no pencil cells, and ferritin may be elevated (acute-phase reaction). This smear picture does not match G6PD.

answers.text: Anaemia of chronic disease — normocytic or mildly microcytic with elevated ferritin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Anaemia of chronic disease typically shows normocytic-normochromic or mildly microcytic anaemia with a NORMAL or elevated ferritin (iron is sequestered, not depleted). The very low ferritin here excludes this diagnosis.

overallFeedback.feedback: Very low ferritin + hypochromic microcytic smear + high RDW = IDA. Thalassaemia trait has normal RDW and ferritin. ACD has normal or elevated ferritin. G6PD shows bite cells.

Correct! IDA smear: hypochromia + microcytosis + pencil cells + high RDW. Very low ferritin confirms. Key distinctions: IDA = high RDW + low ferritin; thalassaemia trait = normal RDW + normal ferritin; ACD = normal/high ferritin.
